hints: Look closely at the atoms at the ends of each pair. What do you see in X (O and H), in Y (only C and H in CH3 groups), and in Z (+ and - charges)?
Remember how R groups interact in tertiary structure: OH groups can share H, non-polar CH3 groups cluster together away from water, and opposite full charges attract strongly.
walkthrough:
**Look at Pair X**

Both side chains end in an -OH group. That means oxygen with hydrogen attached.

O and H together make the group polar and able to form hydrogen bonds. So X is a hydrogen bond.

**Look at Pair Y**

Both side chains show only $CH_3$ methyl groups attached to carbon. There is no O, N or charge here.

C-H groups are non-polar and hydrophobic, so they cluster together by hydrophobic interaction. So Y is a hydrophobic interaction.

**Look at Pair Z and Conclude**

One side shows $NH_3^+$ and the other shows $COO^-$. That is a full positive charge facing a full negative charge.

Opposite charges attract to form an ionic bond, also called a salt bridge. So Z is an ionic bond. That gives X hydrogen bond, Y hydrophobic interaction, Z ionic bond, which is row B.

options.A: Incorrect because X is not hydrophobic. The -OH groups are polar and form hydrogen bonds, not hydrophobic interactions.
options.B: Correct. X with two polar -OH groups forms a hydrogen bond, Y with non-polar CH3 groups forms a hydrophobic interaction, and Z with NH3+ and COO- forms an ionic bond.
options.C: Incorrect because only X forms a hydrogen bond. Y has no polar groups for hydrogen bonding and Z has full opposite charges for ionic bonding.
options.D: Incorrect because X is wrong. The -OH groups are hydrophilic and hydrogen bonding, not hydrophobic, even though Y and Z are correctly named here.
